say: Friend at the fence. Come, stand where the fire shows you.
You again. Good. The little ones count your steps.
Walk easy. Gate knows your face now.
Friend. Hush has spoken of you. That is not nothing here.
Our friend walks. Open the fence a hand.
Meat-bringer. Sit. Be quiet with us a while.
Good, you came. The gate is lighter when you are in it.
Kin of the gate, nearly. Do not tell the Plains.
Slow, stranger. Gate does not know you yet.
No friend of ours. Not yet. Stay on the road side of the fence.
Walk wide. Hush watches strangers longest.
Quiet. Little ones sleep. Gate is not open to you, not yet.
You made the gate close. Go back to the grass.
No more. Hush said no. We say no.
You are not welcome. Hunger is not welcome either, but you are worse.
Gate stays shut for you. Hush says so.
Somebody sits easy with the Gate Folk. Shared a fire with them. I've buried people who did less and I won't say what I think.
They say an outlander walks in and out of that fence like a market stall. I want to see his hands. I want to see under his nails.
A man who eats beside the Gate Folk eats beside the Plains. That's how I see it. I don't argue it, I just stop sitting near him.
Hush keeps her people from the pot. Fine. But who's the stranger who calls her friend? Tell me that and I'll tell you if I trust it.
Did you know a cannibal doesn't eat his friends? Ask yourself what that makes a man who's a friend of cannibals.
I lost a brother on those plains. Now there's a fence up north where savages say sorry in meat and outlanders go shake hands.
I won't say a word against a man who got a cannibal to stop eating. I'll say a lot against what it costs to find out if it worked.
My hands shake when I hear they trade with strangers up there. Not at the Gate. At the strangers. Somebody always walks out wrong.
Half of us leave them be, the Gate lot. The other half haven't lost enough. Someone friendly to them hasn't either.
The Gate is a tamed dog next to a pack. A man who feeds it forgets the pack is still out there.
You smell of the north. Of the fence. Don't tell me you ate there.
I hear you're on good terms with the Gate. Keep it away from me.
Friend of the cannibals? Some of them. I know what you are. I do not like it.
I won't shoot you. I want that understood. I won't drink with you either.
Hush has a friend in you. Good for Hush.
I watched the Gate once from a ridge. They shared bread with a stranger. I did not shoot. I still do not know why.
Careful. The ones at the fence are sorry now. The ones behind it aren't. A friend to one is a mark to the other.
Friendly with the Gate, aye? Then you know what hunger does. I want to hear you say you don't feel it.
You walked in there and walked out. That's more than most. I want to hate you for it.
Gate friend. The word is out. You won't like how it sits with hunters.
You're on the wrong side of this. A cannibal is a cannibal, a fence or no.
Whatever you eat with them, it's on your hands. I won't forget it.
I tolerated you when I didn't know.
A cannibal at the edge of the plains takes meat and gives mercy. Our brothers say it is a trick. Our brothers have not been there.
They say a traveller has made friends with the cannibals. I pray it is a rumour. If not, I pray for his soul and keep a hand on my blade.
Okran sent the Flame to cleanse them. Now one stands in their gate and gives water to strangers. The Book says nothing of this.
Dining with cannibals is not friendship. It is a sin that wears friendship like a hood.
One tamed cannibal is a lamb with a wolf in it. One traveller who trusts her is a fool or a heretic. The Inquisitors will decide which.
I won't say the Gate Folk are saved. I'll say I have heard of no one taken for food there. Is that holy? I don't know the Book well enough.
A priest told us never to hold meat from the Plains. A soldier said it was the best meat he had had. We didn't ask where.
They keep no priests. They keep no rank. Still they have rules. It troubles me more than a pyre would.
Pray the stranger who walks among them returns clean. A man cannot wash that off. He can only stop being a man.
It was in the Book that cannibals are the Flame's meat. It isn't in the Book that one may be forgiven. So who forgave her?
You keep company with the Gate. I will not report it.
Heretic! No. Not heretic. A man who walks among cannibals. I have no word for it.
Okran watch you, stranger. And whoever you share a pot with.
The Gate Folk. They called you friend. I called them abomination. One of us is wrong.
I smell the Plains on you. Wash before you enter a holy house.
The Book calls them beasts. You call them friends. A priest could argue it in a week.
I have no quarrel with a man who feeds the hungry. Even them.
Friend to the cannibals... Does the Flame know? It must. I pray it forgives, or hurries.
Keep it away from us, whatever you do up there. The Holy Nation has enough to cleanse.
Friend of cannibals. The Inquisitors will want to hear about this.
The Gate Folk's friend. Your hands are stained, heretic.
Whoever shares a fire with the Plains shares its fate.
You kept company with the unclean.
You friend of Hush! Dhe traitor's dog! Dhe pot is ungry for dhat!
Dhe Gate Folk's dog! /CANNIBALCURSE/
Friend of dhe weak ones. We make you weak in dhe pot.
You smell like dhe gate. We smell it.
Hush taught you to be soft. Soft is good. Soft meat tender.
Dhe friend of Hush walks dhere. We watch you.
You go to dhe gate? We do not stop you. Not today. Dhe Chief says no.
Dhere he goes, dhe friend of dhe weak. Dhe Plains remember.
Hush's friend. We have a pot waiting for dhat.
Dhere is a stranger who walks into dhe gate and comes out whole. Dhey say Hush likes him. We do not like him.
Dhe gate takes meat from outlanders. Dhey call dhem friends. We call dhem food who walk.
Hush has a pet outlander. Dhe Chief wants him for dhe Chief's pot. Dhe Chief is patient.
Dhe weak ones feed on strangers' charity. Dhat is dhe whole shame of dhem.
Friend of dhe Gate Folk is no friend of ours. Dhat is plain. Dhat is dhe whole of it.
Dhey gave him bread at dhe gate. Bread! We could give him meat. Dhe meat would be him.
Dhe stranger goes north, comes south. Dhe grass whispers where he steps.
I leave bones at dhe fence. Dhe stranger leaves beast. Dhe fence loves him more. I do not mind.
Dhe outlander shakes dhe hand of Hush. I would shake his hand too. Off at dhe wrist.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers. Cannibals, or were. Someone has their trust. A useful man to know, or one to watch.
A friend of the Gate Folk, they say. Not a bad contact. Their toll is only beast meat. I've seen worse partners in the Cities.
Cannibals who deal fair is a contradiction the Empire has yet to rule on. A stranger up north has the ear of them, I hear.
A man who trades with the northern tribe has contacts no guild could buy. I would like an introduction. I would not like to share a table.
Word is a tribe at the edge of the plains takes outsiders. They ask meat for passage. A shrewd toll, if it's as they say.
A stranger got past a cannibal fence in the north. By paying, not fighting. Ask me how that's possible and I'll say the price was fair.
Frontier folk, up past the plains, trade with strangers now. Something in that.
A tribe that trades with whoever walks up. The Cities could learn from them, if the smell was less.
Somewhere north, a tribe trades with strangers. Or traded. Or they ate them. The story changes with the bar.
A hungry tribe on the plains that doesn't eat the passerby. I'd pay to see a contract with them.
The north has a trader who's a cannibal, or a cannibal who's a trader. The ledger doesn't say.
I heard cannibals sell hospitality. Surely that isn't legal. Surely that isn't cheap.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers. Raw meat for safe passage. Cheapest toll on the road, and I'd pay it twice.
Somebody has the Gate Folk's trust. That is a better insurance than any bodyguard. I would like to hear his rates.
I took the northern road last season. Fence at the edge of the plains. They took my meat and didn't take my cart. I call that service.
There's a man who does business with cannibals now. I wonder what his margin is. I wonder what the margin has cost.
Word is a tribe at the edge of the plains deals with strangers. Cannibals, once. They keep a toll in beast meat.
A fence in the north where a caravan can stop and not be eaten. Never thought I'd say that as a recommendation.
The Gate toll is cheap, they say. Cheap and humane. If you can afford the stomach for it.
I heard the plains have a safe spot now. A little one. I haven't seen a map with it.
Up on the plains somebody trades with strangers. It could be a market. It could be a pot.
A cannibal who takes meat and gives safe passage. A pretty tale. Pretty tales are how caravans disappear.
North of here, a toll gate run by people who ought to be eating me. I'm told it's honest.
Somebody has a deal with the plains. I don't know who. I'd like to ask what they paid.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers. They keep nobody in chains. I wanted to be sure. They don't, and I don't know what to do with that.
The Gate Folk take no slaves, they say. A stranger is friends with them. I trust him a little more for it, and I hate myself for it.
A camp of cannibals that frees people instead of eating them. I won't call it good. I won't call it evil. I'll call it an exception.
I wouldn't tell my squad. Some of them would walk there to see. I'd be one of them.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers and keeps no slaves. A fine thing, if it's true. Most fine things aren't.
I heard cannibals who shelter the hungry. We shelter the hungry. Maybe we have more in common than I wished to know.
The north has a gate. They ask only meat. Beast meat. I'll believe it when someone not dead says so.
No cages at that fence, they say. I want to see a camp with no cages and not wonder where they hide them.
A tribe of the plains that does not hurt strangers. It cannot be. I want to see it. I will not go.
Somewhere north there's a cannibal camp where nobody is sold. If this is a trick, it's a good one.
People say a hungry people stopped eating people. Even the Slavers heard of it.
A cannibal gate, a free road. A story for children who need to believe in something.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers. /FLATSKIN/ who ate /FLATSKIN/ and put it down. Their warrior-woman walks like a Shek, so I hear.
A /FLATSKIN/ among us is friends with the Gate Folk. I won't mock him. A tribe that dares leave its sins is worth a handshake.
The Gate Folk keep the old courtesies, in their way. A guest is not eaten. That is honour. It is not Shek honour.
Kral's Chosen would laugh at me, but I say it: the Gate is a better border than any fort I have held.
There's a tribe past the Cannibal Plains that trades with those who ask. A strange thing, in a strange land.
A fence in the north where the hungry are fed and the cruel aren't. It sounds Shek. It isn't, but it sounds it.
A gate keeper who guards with courage and not with cruelty. I'd drink to her. I haven't met her.
The Gate Folk don't hunt guests. This is a rule of a good people. I didn't expect to find it on the plains.
Somewhere in the north, cannibals who respect a stranger. I'll believe it when I see it, and I won't go see it.
I heard there's a tribe that trades. A tribe, trading. Among the flatskins this is rarer than a Stone Golem's smile.
A people of the plains grew tired of eating. A good tale. A short one, sadly.
I heard cannibals gave a Shek bread. I don't know the Shek. Perhaps I do.
Query: a tribe exists at the edge of the plains. It trades with strangers. It doesn't harm travellers who pay. Observed.
A person of flesh is friend to the Gate Folk. The Gate Folk are cannibals. This is acceptable. They have no use for Skeletons.
The tribe has accepted trade. The tribe has no reason to accept us. We don't mind.
Flesh, no flesh. The Gate Folk don't differ. Seen once.
Report: a tribe on the plains permits trade. Intent: unknown. Danger: low, if not carrying meat that isn't beast.
A fence in the north. People who guard it don't attack. We have been told.
A tribe of flesh doesn't eat flesh. Flagged as anomaly.
No cause to avoid the Gate. No cause to approach. Notation entered.
Unverified: cannibals trade with strangers at the edge of the plains. Source: a drunk.
A cannibal tribe that does not eat people. This is not a thing. Data is inconsistent.
North: a tribe. Behaviour: peaceful. Probability: unclear. Remaining observations: none.
They say flesh will stop eating flesh. We haven't seen it.
A tribe stands at the edge of the plains and trades with strangers. They were cannibals. They put the hunger down.
We hear that a traveller shares meat with the gate keeper. The gate keeper shares water. This is how a hive begins, perhaps.
The Gate Folk don't hunt the lost. We understand. We have also been lost and been found.
A tribe that takes in the hungry. We would walk there, if our Queen allowed. She doesn't forbid it. She doesn't know of it.
There's a tribe past the plains that trades with outsiders. We have heard it from many mouths. It's a quiet tale.
A people of the north, once eaters, now keepers of a gate. We hope the gate holds.
They guard against their own kind. It is a hard thing.
A tribe that doesn't eat what passes. We would greet them. They might not greet us.
We hear of a tribe at the edge of the plains. It's a small tale. It has been passed along without being changed, which is rare.
North, a gate. A hungry tribe behind it. It trades, it doesn't eat. We're told this by those who passed.
A tribe that's also a choice. We hope it's true. We have no way to know.
Many lost souls, one gate. We would learn their song if they have one.
Word is you deal with the Gate Folk. Cats are cats. Meat is, I suppose, also a currency.
A friend of the northern tribe. Handy. Does it come with a price?
The Cities don't judge who you trade with. The Cities do keep records.
A man who walks into the Gate and returns can name his price. What's yours?
You deal with the Gate Folk? Not a bad route if the meat is fresh.
Friend of the northern tribe. Are they buying? Are they selling? Tell me nothing, I know already.
A trader who's welcome where nobody is welcome. Do you carry for hire?
I have asked about the Gate. Few return with an answer.
You walk with the Gate Folk. I checked what they do with strangers. I was relieved.
A friend of cannibals. I have friends in worse places. Not many.
If the Gate keeps nobody in chains, they and we aren't enemies. That's the sum of it.
I won't judge a man by the camp he feeds. I'll judge him by who he frees.
I hear you're a friend of the Gate Folk. A /FLATSKIN/ who earns the trust of the hungry. It's no small thing.
The Gate keeper has honour. You have her trust. The Stone Golem sees both.
A friend of those who stopped eating their own. A good name to carry, even if it smells.
Few flatskins break bread with the plains. You do. I'll watch what you become.
Query: you're accepted by the Gate Folk. Query: is that useful? Answer: unknown.
Observation: your relation with the northern tribe is positive.
The Gate Folk don't harm you. They won't harm us. Probable.
Flesh friend. Gate friend. Both labels accepted.
We have heard you are friend to the people at the gate. We are glad. A friend is a rare thing.
You walk with the tribe of the north. We don't fear.
The gate people trust you. We would learn why. Perhaps you would tell us.
It's good to be trusted by the hungry. We know it a little.
Gate Folk country. They know us here, so they say. I still do not like the smell of smoke.
The fence is ahead. We're known at it. I keep a hand on my sword anyway.
Don't stare. Don't ask what's in the pot. Gate has meat, they said.
At least the savages up here talk first.
Gate Folk land. They have a word for us now. Friend. I'll take it, for as long as it lasts.
Quiet. We're guests. Stay off the grass that looks tended.
A friend in these woods is worth three swords.
The little ones watch us. I do not like it. I do not stop them.
We know the Gate people. They like us. I try not to wonder why.
Please don't touch anything. Please don't look at the cages.
They're kind, I think. They seem kind. It's so hard to tell.
If anyone offers me stew, I'm going to be sick.
The Gate Folk honour their guests. This is an old courtesy. The Shek understand it.
Let us be good guests. We bring meat. They bring peace. This is a fair trade.
A people who once ate. A people who stopped. The Shek respect strength.
Keep your spear down. We're known here.
We're known to this people. We're glad. We won't stay long.
The air is thick with smoke. The people here are quiet. We'll be quiet too.
They share meat with those who share meat. We're among them.
The gate people watch. We watch back.
Observation: Gate Folk territory. Relation: positive.
Query: expected duration of stay? Answer: short.
Gate Folk are cannibals. They aren't cannibalising.
Nothing has attacked. Probability of ambush: reduced.
Gate Folk ground. They accept us. The Sun looks down on this and doesn't turn away.
I've walked into worse. This is calmer, if only slightly.
A people who stopped eating people. I've known less honest ones with more gold.
I do not trust them. I trust the fence.
I'm starving and this is the worst place to say it. I know.
If the savages here ask for meat I'll have nothing. I'll have to give them me.
Everything smells like food and I don't want to know what kind.
Tell me we brought something. Anything. Not raw. Not meat.
If the Gate wants meat, I have none. My stomach doesn't either.
Hungry. Very. Don't tempt me with their toll.
I'd trade my boots for a bone right now. I mean the animal kind.
I know where the meat is up here. I don't want to know.
I'm so hungry. I don't want to be near the cooking. I don't want to be near the cooks.
Please, anything. Not from them. Not from here.
My stomach is eating itself and this is the one place I can't ask.
I'd rather starve than ask. Remind me I said that.
Hunger is a trial. This place is a worse one.
A warrior who starves shames his King. A warrior who eats here shames himself.
I'll hunt for it. Keep the Gate away from my back.
Starving, and surrounded by a people who understand hunger. Fitting.
We're hungry. We would eat. We would eat beast.
Hunger is shared in the hive. Here it isn't.
We need food. We don't want it from them. We don't want to ask.
We have wandered hungry before. We'll again.
Observation: food reserves insufficient. Cause: travel. Not an issue for me.
Query: why are the organics distressed? Answer: hunger.
Query: do the Gate Folk share meat with the starving. Answer: they ask for it.
Hunger isn't a concern. Yours is.
Hungry. Do not ask me to eat anything the Gate Folk offer.
The Sun gives warmth. It doesn't give meat. I have to find some.
Hungry, in a place full of hungry people. At least the company is honest.
I'm hungry enough to eat anything. Here, that's a sentence I shouldn't say.
The Gate folk know us. Doesn't mean the rest of the plains does.
Friends to one tribe, meat to another.
We have a name in the north. Here it's a different one.
A friend at the fence is no help on the grass.
Gate Folk friend or not, these are still the plains.
I know a safe spot up north. I don't know how to get there past all this.
A friend in the Gate and a hundred enemies in the grass.
We hold a name the Chief will not like.
Please can we just go north to the Gate. They know us there.
I was told the Gate Folk are the kind ones. Please let me find them first.
The gate people will know us. I hope.
I want to be at the fence. I want the fence between me and all of this.
Friends to the gate means enemies to the plains.
The Chief will want us. Let him find us ready.
We bear the Gate's name through enemy ground. It's a heavy gift.
A Shek can walk through any grass.
We're friends of the gate people. The others won't be our friends.
The plains are watching. We watch the plains. It's a long watch.
We have a name among the quiet cannibals. It won't be a quiet name here.
Move together. We're marked.
Observation: this faction hostile. The other faction friendly.
Query: how long to the fence? Answer: unknown.
I carry no flesh. I'm of no interest to them.
Probability of attack: high. Reaction plan: run north.
Friend of the Gate, enemy of the plains. Ha. It could be worse.
We have to get to the fence. The fence is a long way. Keep your head down.
I've walked through worse. I don't remember where.
The Sun is out. So are they. Walk fast.
You carry someone. Not meat. Put them down or Hush will ask why.
That one on your back. Alive? Not kin? Not meat? Hush wants to know.
Do not bring that to the fence. Not here.
We do not eat people. We also do not carry them.
You carry someone. Friend, we do not ask. We ask only that they are not for any pot.
Friend, whoever you carry, they stay outside the fence.
Your burden is your own. Do not bring it past the gate.
A person on your back. Alive? Then they have a right to say.
You carry a person. Hush would not like it. We do not ask. Not yet.
Friend. That one you carry. Where do you take them? Not to the pot.
Put them down before the gate.
A body in your arms. We do not eat people.
You carry a person! Resh! Sell! Sell for coin! /CANNIBALCOIN/
Dhat one you carry. Looks tasty. Looks tender. How much?
Dhat is meat dhat walks! Give it, or we take it with you!
You bring us a gift! Dhank you!
Whoever you carry, don't take them north. There are worse fates than being a slave.
A person on your back near the plains. I don't like it. I want to hear why.
Is that one for the cannibals? Say no. Say it fast.
I've seen too many carried that way into the grass. Don't do it.
You carry a heretic? A slave? A sinner? I do not ask, but the Flame will.
A person in your arms and you walk toward the plains. Be sure of what you do.
If that one is for the pot, I'll see you burn.
Whatever you carry, do not give it to the savages.
